memos.headline: CAT and UNH Lead on Relative Strength; MSFT and XOM in Technical Distress
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. CAT is at its 52-week high with +60.2% over 26 weeks, +12.2% 4-week relative strength vs SPY, and RSI at 65.4—parabolic but not yet overbought enough to fade; I'd stay long but tighten stops below the 50-day (~$873). UNH is the standout momentum name with +47.3% over 12 weeks, only -2.9% from its high, and massive +32.9% 12-week relative strength vs SPY; trend is intact above the 50-day. On the other side, MSFT is deeply broken—30% off its 52-week high, 15.9% below its 200-day mean, RSI at 34.9, and bleeding relative strength at -10.6% over 4 weeks vs SPY; I see no reason to step in front of this until it reclaims at least the 50-day (~$413). XOM is similarly ugly with RSI 32.9, -19.6% drawdown, and the worst 12-week relative strength in the group at -31.0% vs SPY; avoid until it stabilizes above $145.

views.note: At 52-week highs with dominant relative strength across all timeframes; would reassess on a close below $873 (approximate 50-day mean).
Exceptional 12-week momentum of +47.3% with +32.9% relative strength vs SPY and only -2.9% from highs; trend intact above the 50-day.
Healthy trend with +7.7% 4-week return, RSI 62, only -2.8% from highs, and positive 4-week relative strength; would turn neutral below $308 (approximate 50-day).
Strong 12-week relative strength (+12.4% vs SPY) but 4-week weakness of -5.4% and RSI near 49 suggest consolidation; wait for a reclaim above the 50-day to add.
Sitting right at the 50-day with neutral RSI of 50.9 and modest -2.1% 4-week relative strength; no edge either way until it breaks above $315 or below $285.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Post Extraordinary Earnings Growth; XOM and UNH Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I am struck by the sheer dispersion in earnings quality across this universe. NVDA's 2027Q1 filing shows $81.6B in revenue (+85% YoY) and a 71.5% net margin producing $58.3B of net income (+211% YoY) on only $8.5B of total debt—this is the cleanest earnings power profile I see today. GOOGL delivered $62.6B of net income on a 56.9% net margin with revenue up 21.8% YoY and minimal leverage at $14.8B of debt, which is remarkable operating leverage. On the other end, XOM's net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to $4.2B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin, and UNH grew revenue only 2.0% with net income essentially flat at $6.3B against $77.9B of debt—both signal durable earnings headwinds. CAT surprised me positively with 22.2% revenue growth and 14.6% margins, though I want to see whether the backlog sustains before raising conviction further.

views.note: Revenue +85% YoY, net margin 71.5%, net income +211% YoY on minimal $8.5B debt is the strongest earnings power in the universe; would reassess if margins compress below 60%.
Net income +81% YoY to $62.6B with 56.9% margin and only $14.8B debt shows exceptional operating leverage; a deceleration in ad revenue growth below 10% would change my view.
Revenue +18.3% YoY, 38.3% net margin, and net income +23.1% with manageable $40.3B debt reflect durable cloud-driven earnings growth.
Net income surged 76.7% YoY to $30.3B and margin expanded to 16.7%, but $122.6B of total debt and heavy capex needs temper my conviction; margin contraction below 12% would flip me neutral.
Revenue +22.2% and net income +27.2% YoY with 14.6% margins are strong, but cyclicality and $36.2B debt versus $17.4B quarterly revenue warrant caution until backlog visibility improves.
Revenue +16.6% and 26.6% margin are solid but $82.7B of debt is the highest among tech peers here; I need to see services mix continue expanding to get more constructive.
Revenue +10% and 33.1% net margin are respectable for a bank, but the rate cycle outlook and $449B debt load limit upside conviction.
Steady 7.4% revenue growth and 18.5% margin offer defensive value, but low earnings growth of 4.3% YoY doesn't justify paying up.
Net income down 45.8% YoY to $4.2B on a 4.9% margin signals severe earnings compression; would reconsider only if margins recover above 10%.
Revenue growth of just 2.0% and flat net income at $6.3B against $77.9B of debt point to stalling earnings power; need to see medical cost ratio improve before reconsidering.

memos.headline: Fed Paused at 3.75% but Sticky 4.2% YoY CPI and Rising Long Rates Squeeze Duration and Favor Defensives
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly on pause—upper bound at 3.75%, unchanged over three months despite 75 bps of cuts over the past year—because headline CPI is running at +4.2% YoY (May print 333.98), well above any comfort zone for further easing. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.3%, down 10 bps over three months and flat YoY, so there is no urgency to cut further. The 10-year yield has risen 20 bps over three months to 4.46%, while the 10y-2y spread has compressed 23 bps to just +0.29 pp, signaling the market is repricing for higher-for-longer rates and possibly slower growth ahead. This regime—paused policy, sticky inflation, flattening curve—is negative for long-duration growth equities and constructive for banks earning on a still-positive curve and for defensive staples. A CPI print falling below 3.5% YoY or unemployment rising above 4.6% would shift my call toward renewed easing and a more risk-on posture.

views.note: Long-duration consumer tech equity is pressured by rising real rates and a 10y yield at 4.46% with no near-term easing catalyst.
Quality growth with recurring revenue offers some buffer, but higher-for-longer rates cap multiple expansion; staying neutral until curve or inflation regime shifts.
Highest-duration name in the universe faces the most headwind from a 20 bps rise in the 10y and sticky 4.2% inflation keeping the Fed on hold.
Banks benefit from a still-positive 10y-2y spread of 29 bps, stable employment at 4.3%, and a paused Fed that keeps net interest margins predictable.
Defensive staples with pricing power are well-suited to a sticky-inflation, late-cycle pause regime where unemployment is stable but growth is decelerating.
Energy is a natural inflation hedge but the flattening curve hints at slowing demand; I lack conviction either way without clearer growth signals.
Cyclicals face headwinds from a flattening curve (10y-2y down 23 bps in 3 months) and higher borrowing costs dampening capex.
Mixed exposure—AWS is duration-sensitive but retail benefits from stable employment; net effect is roughly neutral in a pause regime.
Ad revenue is cyclically sensitive and higher rates weigh on the multiple, but strong cash generation provides a floor; neutral until macro regime clarifies.
Defensive healthcare with stable demand benefits from a late-cycle pause; low unemployment supports employer-sponsored enrollment.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: GOOGL and CAT Surged, MSFT and NVDA Sold Off — Narrative Momentum Favors the Winners
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions and subsequent 8-K filing cadence as proxies for sentiment direction across the universe. GOOGL (+10.0%) and CAT (+9.9%) posted the strongest earnings-day pops, and both have seen sustained corporate activity since (GOOGL with six additional 8-Ks through June 11 including material agreements and board changes, CAT with a June 11 Reg FD disclosure), suggesting the positive narrative has legs and management is leaning into it. MSFT's -3.9% earnings reaction and two subsequent director departure filings signal a tone that has not recovered, while NVDA's -1.8% post-print fade combined with two director departures in late April/early May raises questions about internal stability. AAPL's +3.2% pop was clean but the filing trail has gone quiet since April 30, which I read as neutral — the good news is priced. I have lower conviction on names like UNH and XOM where the filing flow is routine and the earnings reactions were muted or negative.

views.note: Strongest earnings reaction in the universe at +10.0% followed by a dense stream of material agreements and governance filings through mid-June, suggesting sustained positive narrative momentum.
A +9.9% earnings-day move was the second-best in the universe, and the June 11 Reg FD disclosure suggests management is actively guiding sentiment higher.
The -3.9% earnings reaction was the worst in the group, and two subsequent director departure filings without any positive catalysts suggest the negative tone has not inflected.
A -1.8% post-earnings fade plus two director departures in the weeks prior point to unsettled sentiment; I see no clear positive inflection yet.
The +3.2% earnings pop was solid but the absence of any follow-on filings since April 30 suggests the good news is fully absorbed.
A modest +0.8% earnings reaction and subsequent material agreement/debt obligation filings are mixed signals — not enough directional conviction.
The -1.0% earnings reaction was mild and subsequent filings are routine governance; no sentiment catalyst visible.
High filing volume but all governance and 'Other Events' — no earnings reaction data provided and no clear tone shift.
A +1.7% earnings pop is modest and the Reg FD filing the same day suggests guidance was in-line; sentiment is flat.
Only a Reg FD disclosure and a shareholder vote filing — too little signal to form a directional sentiment view.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Easing but Oil Collapse and Yield Curve Flattening Signal Unresolved Geopolitical Crosscurrents
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 29% month-over-month to 333.6, suggesting some near-term de-escalation in trade or sanctions rhetoric, though the level remains elevated at +2.6% over three months—this is not a structural all-clear. WTI crude at $80.65 is down 26% in a single month and 16% over three months, which I read as either a demand shock or a significant supply-side geopolitical shift (e.g., eased sanctions on a major producer or OPEC+ discipline breakdown); either interpretation has differentiated implications across the universe. HY spreads at 2.63% (tightening 59bp over 3m) and VIX at 18.44 (down ~18% over 3m) tell me credit markets are not pricing a hard-landing scenario, but the 10y-2y spread compressing 23bp to just 0.29pp over three months keeps me cautious on duration-sensitive financials. I have moderate conviction on names with clear geopolitical exposure—energy, industrials with China/infrastructure linkage, and big tech facing export-control risk—but limited conviction elsewhere given the absence of specific policy catalysts in the 8-K filings available to me.

views.note: The 26% one-month WTI collapse suggests either demand destruction or a geopolitical supply release that structurally pressures upstream margins.
No new export-control signals in available evidence, but elevated baseline policy uncertainty (+2.6% 3m) and China semiconductor restrictions remain a structural overhang I cannot dismiss.
Two Reg FD filings in six weeks suggest active investor engagement, and easing policy uncertainty supports global infrastructure capex, though I would reverse on any new tariff escalation.
Tightening HY spreads are positive for credit quality, but the 23bp compression in the 10y-2y spread to 0.29pp squeezes net interest margin and limits upside.
Three 8-K filings since May including Reg FD disclosure suggest proactive positioning; falling policy uncertainty benefits ad-driven revenue, though antitrust and China policy remain tail risks.

Defensive consumer staples benefit from lower uncertainty, but a strong dollar scenario from flattening yields could pressure international earnings; insufficient geopolitical signal to take a directional view.
